nodes.label: Admin Template
nodes.rationale: Derived by filtering rather than listed by hand, so a new admin page is picked up automatically while the Roles page stays excluded.

nodes.label: Bootstrap via create-admin
nodes.rationale: Finds the super-admin role by permission rather than by name, creating it from the template only when none exists.

nodes.label: Roles Page Keys Hidden From the Editor
nodes.norm_label: roles page keys hidden from the editor
nodes.rationale: Absent rather than greyed out, so no admin can grant the restricted key through the interface at all.

nodes.label: Role Templates
nodes.rationale: Pre-checked defaults only; never saved as records, so a created role keeps no connection to the template it came from.

nodes.label: Super Admin Template
nodes.rationale: The only template including the Roles page keys, and what the bootstrap script reads on a fresh server.

nodes.label: RBAC Locked Decisions
nodes.rationale: Written as locked decisions so permission work does not re-litigate settled design each time it is touched.

nodes.label: Primary and Foreign Key Naming
nodes.rationale: Semantic foreign key names are allowed where the name does not match the referenced table, documented inline in the schema file.

nodes.label: Snake Case Columns, Camel Case Fields
nodes.norm_label: snake case columns, camel case fields
nodes.rationale: Mapped in the Drizzle schema so the database and TypeScript each keep their own convention.

nodes.label: Soft Delete via Status Enum
nodes.rationale: A status enum rather than a boolean flag, so more than two lifecycle states stay expressible.

nodes.label: Protection From a Live Condition, Not a Column
nodes.norm_label: protection from a live condition, not a column
nodes.rationale: There is no protection flag column; protection is derived by asking whether the role currently holds the roles-management key.

nodes.label: Open: Surfacing Role Contents Outside the Roles Page
nodes.norm_label: open: surfacing role contents outside the roles page
nodes.rationale: A user manager assigns roles by name alone; a popover listing the selected role permissions is the likely fix.

nodes.label: Roles Editor Is Super-Admin Only
nodes.rationale: View is withheld alongside manage because a Roles page nobody can edit has no reason to exist, so the read-only rendering is never built.

nodes.label: Fully Offline LAN Deployment
nodes.rationale: No CDN assets, external auth providers, or runtime network calls, because the server runs on an isolated LAN.

nodes.label: Read Schema and Brief Only When Relevant
nodes.norm_label: read schema and brief only when relevant
nodes.rationale: The schema must be read fresh before any query or migration rather than worked from a remembered copy.

nodes.label: Commit Primary Changes Scope
nodes.rationale: Stages only the files created or modified while completing the current session's task, named one by one instead of git add -A. When the session holds no completed task the files may have changed for reasons never observed, so the correct move is to ask which files are primary rather than guess.

nodes.label: Commit Staged Files Scope
nodes.rationale: Commits exactly the existing index, read with git diff --cached --name-only, and stages nothing new. When the index is empty the run stops and says so rather than guessing at something to add.

nodes.label: Commit This Scope
nodes.rationale: The default when no scope is named: git add -A sweeps modified, deleted, and untracked files. Whatever got swept in that is not the main work is called out in the trailing bullet, and a file that should not be in the repo at all is named and left out rather than committed quietly.

nodes.label: Pre-Commit Format Check
nodes.rationale: A closing checklist re-verifies the staging scope, the prefix and lowercase title, the blank line after it, main-before-unrelated ordering, a bullet or two-space wrap on every body line, the 72-character limit, and the absence of trailers.

nodes.label: No Commit Trailers
nodes.rationale: No Co-Authored-By trailer and no generated-with footer are permitted anywhere in the message.

nodes.label: Bullet Body
nodes.rationale: The body is bullets only, wrapped at 72 characters with two-space continuation indents, one bullet per logical change, three to six bullets in total. Identifiers are written out literally. A commit that needs more than six bullets is probably doing too much and should be split.

nodes.label: Commit Message Format
nodes.rationale: The repo enforces one house shape for commit messages so history stays scannable: a conventional prefix and short lowercase title, a blank line, then a wrapped bullet list. Prose paragraphs are rejected because they bury several logical changes in one block.

nodes.label: Conventional Prefix Title
nodes.rationale: The title takes a conventional prefix (feat, fix, refactor, chore, docs, test), a lowercase first letter, no trailing period, and stays under about 72 characters. Previously untracked files are feat rather than refactor, because nothing existed yet to refactor.

nodes.label: Default Body Ordering
nodes.rationale: Main changes come first, most important first, then anything swept into the same commit that is not part of that work. Trailing bullets stay short; an unrelated change big enough to need its own explanation belongs in its own commit instead.

nodes.label: Staging Scope
nodes.rationale: Which files get staged is settled before the message is written, because the wrong scope forces an amend or a reset afterwards. Three phrases select the scope and the widest one is also the default; the scope is never widened on the agent's own initiative.

nodes.label: Never Zero Active Super-Admins
nodes.rationale: Any action dropping the count to zero is blocked; going from two down to one warns but is allowed.

nodes.label: No User Changes Their Own Role
nodes.norm_label: no user changes their own role
nodes.rationale: Prevents both self-promotion and self-lockout, where an admin strips their own access to the only page that could undo it.

nodes.label: Exactly One Holder of the Restricted Key
nodes.norm_label: exactly one holder of the restricted key
nodes.rationale: Enforced as a safety net against a bypassed request, since the interface already makes the key unreachable.

nodes.label: Only a Super-Admin Assigns Super-Admin
nodes.rationale: Together with the self-change rule this closes the grant path: a user manager can neither promote themselves nor a colleague, and unassignment is restricted the same way.

nodes.label: Super-Admin Role
nodes.rationale: Identified by holding the roles-management key rather than by name, since names are editable runtime data.

nodes.label: Expand Permissions Walks the Whole Chain
nodes.norm_label: expand permissions walks the whole chain
nodes.rationale: PERMISSION_IMPLIES stores single steps only, and expansion is idempotent, so it is safe to apply anywhere.

nodes.label: Frozen Super-Admin Role
nodes.rationale: Only the description is editable; name, status, and the permission set are locked, and deletion, deactivation, and duplication are blocked.

nodes.label: Implied Permissions
nodes.rationale: Unrecognised keys pass through untouched rather than being dropped, so a leftover database row never silently removes access it was already granting.

nodes.label: Open: Orphan Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Orphans are removed by hand today; whether the sync script should offer deletion is undecided and not urgent.

nodes.label: Orphan Keys Reported, Never Deleted
nodes.rationale: The join table is declared without a delete cascade, so MySQL restricts the delete; clearing an orphan means removing live role grants first, which is not a decision a script should make unattended.

nodes.label: Permission Sync
nodes.rationale: Permission rows are data, not schema, so the migration generator produces nothing for a new key and this script is what puts it into the database.

nodes.label: Super-Admin Backfill
nodes.rationale: Required because the frozen role has no interface path to gain a new module.

nodes.label: Admin Role Kind
nodes.rationale: Admin roles hold only admin keys because a staff permission is unusable to a user whose navigation is confined to the admin routes.

nodes.label: Mirrored Admin and Staff Data Routes
nodes.norm_label: mirrored admin and staff data routes
nodes.rationale: Kept as separate routes rather than one route branching on permissions, because the admin table has features the staff table does not and merging them would tangle two interfaces.

nodes.label: Open: Staff Module Actions Beyond View
nodes.norm_label: open: staff module actions beyond view
nodes.rationale: Blocked on deciding whether encoder-submitted data needs approval before it counts toward reports.

nodes.label: Check Permission Keys, Never Role Names
nodes.norm_label: check permission keys, never role names
nodes.rationale: Role names are runtime data an admin can rename, while keys are defined in source and cannot change underneath the code.

nodes.label: User to Role to Permission Model
nodes.norm_label: user to role to permission model
nodes.rationale: One role per user with no per-user overrides; a person needing a different set gets a duplicated role instead.

nodes.label: Keys Built Forward, Never Split Apart
nodes.norm_label: keys built forward, never split apart
nodes.rationale: The underscore is both the separator and a legal character inside a submodule name, so a finished key cannot be parsed back into its parts unambiguously.

nodes.label: Mandatory View Action Per Module
nodes.rationale: Each route load function checks the module view key, so a module without one is unreachable by anybody.

nodes.label: One Level of Submodules
nodes.rationale: Deeper nesting would make the action-first flattening ambiguous.

nodes.label: Permission Key Shape
nodes.rationale: PERMISSION_DEFS is the single source, so a new module or action is added in exactly one place.

nodes.label: Role Editor Auto-Tick
nodes.rationale: Managing a page you cannot open is meaningless, so any non-view action ticks its module view, and unticking view clears the module.

nodes.label: Server-Side Expansion Before Writing
nodes.rationale: The browser can be bypassed, so expanding on the server means the database can never reach a state the interface would not have produced.
